design.affected_system: urban drainage, stormwater, and flood-response system
alternatives: stage pumps from forecast catchment loads
use rolling event forecasts with conservative capacity reserves
assumptions: Rainfall, terrain, drainage, and complaint records use explicit spatial and temporal supports.
Hydraulic capacities and intervention effects remain measured inputs or labeled assumptions.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: Crews and pumps follow ordinary wet-weather activation levels.

constraints.description: The forecast must distinguish routine service calls from verified emergency response tasks.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: event-triggered and reviewed at the stated decision horizon
design.decision_owner: stormwater utility director and emergency-management lead
design.decision_question: What range of pumping, road-closure, and resident-assistance demand follows the forecast rainfall envelope?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The forecast must distinguish routine service calls from verified emergency response tasks.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Held-out storms meet declared event-total, peak-timing, and interval-coverage diagnostics.
independence_key.primary_outcome: response tasks above available event capacity

design.intended_claim: A versioned forecast design for comparing declared alternatives affecting event-level stormwater response demand, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: response tasks above available event capacity
distributional gap in response tasks above available event capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not present forecast operational demand as predicted flood depth or property damage.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Held-out storms meet declared event-total, peak-timing, and interval-coverage diagnostics.

design.title: Forecast rainfall-runoff response demand
transportability_risks: Drainage standards, imperviousness, topography, tides, and maintenance regimes differ.
Complaint density may reflect reporting access rather than flood incidence.

family.affected_system: urban drainage, stormwater, and flood-response system
claim_boundary: Hazard observations and modeled exposure do not establish individual harm or causation.
Proposed adaptations are planning alternatives, not adopted policy or engineered designs.
A design-only record is not a city execution, validated forecast, or impact result.
family.decision_owner: stormwater utility director and emergency-management lead
family.description: Decision designs for drainage diagnosis, rainfall-runoff workload, green infrastructure, response deployment, maintenance timing, compound flooding, and causal evaluation.
family.title: Flood and stormwater resilience

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
